`Dialog.test.ts` tests the backdrop: its element and role, `hidden` and `inert` with `keepMounted`, `forceRender` for a nested dialog, a press on it that closes the dialog and keeps the focus, and its leave in a `<Transition>`.

`Dialog.test.ts` tests the close button: a press closes with `close-press`, a disabled button closes nothing, and a press on the button of a closed dialog emits nothing. A listener cancels a close with `details.cancel()`.
`Dialog.test.ts` tests the description: the popup names it in `aria-describedby`, the last mounted one wins (VUE-45), and an attribute of the developer wins.

`Dialog.test.ts` tests the popup: its element and attributes, the first focus, `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`, the return of the focus (BUG-5519, BUG-6037), the Tab order, the nested state and the error with no root. The arrow keys need no code (test/measurements/dialog.test.ts, D10).
`Dialog.test.ts` tests the portal: `keepMounted`, `to`, a `null` target and `disabled` (VUE-128). The portal renders no element of its own, so its `render` and `className` have no element.

`Dialog.test.ts` tests the handle: triggers outside the root, `open(id)`, `open(null)`, an unknown id, `openWithPayload()`, `close()`, `isOpen`, a handle with no root, a root that gets or loses its handle, two mounted roots with one handle, and a `<Suspense>` that replaces a page.

`Dialog.test.ts` tests the root through the parts: the open state with each reason, `v-model:open` and `v-model:trigger-id`, `cancel()`, the close action, each value of `modal`, the dismissal, the focus, nested dialogs and the stack. `Dialog.hydration.test.ts` tests the server render.
`Dialog.test.ts` tests the title: the popup names it in `aria-labelledby`, the last mounted one wins (VUE-45), and an attribute of the developer wins.

`Dialog.test.ts` tests the trigger: its element and attributes, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` while the popup is in the document (VUE-73), a disabled trigger, Enter and Space on an element that is not a button, and the error with no root.
`Dialog.test.ts` tests the viewport: its role, `hidden` and `inert` with `keepMounted`, `inert` while its popup leaves, the nested states, and a press on it that closes the dialog.
`Dialog.spec.ts` tests the types of the handle and its payload, the slot of the root, the details and the element of a template ref.
Listen to `@after-enter` and `@after-leave` of the `<Transition>` around the popup. They run after its animations end.
A template ref of the root has `close()`. To keep the popup until a JavaScript animation ends, give `:css="false"` to the `<Transition>` around it, and call `done` in its `leave` hook.
The trigger reads its element to know if it is a native button, so it needs no `nativeButton`.
The button reads its element to know if it is a native button, so it needs no `nativeButton`.
The portal is a `<Teleport>` and renders no element, so it has no `as` and no `element` slot. Put an element in the portal when you need one.

A `<Transition>` around the backdrop animates it, in place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and the `transitionStatus` of the state. A closed backdrop leaves the DOM, or has `[hidden]` with `keepMounted`, so it needs no `data-open` and `data-closed`.

A `<Transition>` around the popup animates it, in place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and the `transitionStatus` of the state. A closed popup leaves the DOM, or has `[hidden]` with `keepMounted`, so it needs no `data-open` and `data-closed`.

The viewport is new in the DOM at each open, so a CSS animation on it runs at the open. `:has(> .v-leave-active)` selects it while its popup leaves, and `[hidden]` while `keepMounted` keeps it closed. These take the place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`, `data-open`, `data-closed` and the `transitionStatus` of the state.

surfaceAdditions.reason: The portal is a `<Teleport>`. With `disabled`, it renders its content in place, also in the server HTML.
The portal is a `<Teleport>`. With `defer`, it moves its content after the rest of the update mounted, so its target can come later in the same template.
The part reads `disabled` for its state and for `useButton`, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the trigger, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.
